newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end sharply lower, hit by rate blues.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply lower, hit by rate blues.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended with heavy losses on Friday as comments made by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan earlier this week returned to haunt the market.
The Hang Seng Index tumbled 147.88 points, or 1.09 percent, to 13,398.72. Turnover was a hefty HK$11.64 billion compared with HK$10.85 billion on Thursday.
Over the week, the index fell 46.13 points, or 0.34 percent.
"The market is just nervous about interest rates for the time being," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Greenspan said on Wednesday that the Fed may need to raise rates in coming months. Investors shrugged off the comments on Thursday.
"I think people were a little bit too quick to dismiss what Greenspan said. It is beginning to sink in a little," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading at CS First Boston.
"The (U.S.) bond market was a bit weak so I think people are beginning to realise that there could be an interest rate rise. I think there is a very strong possibility that rates will tick up a bit."
The U.S. long bond fell 12/32 on Thursday to yield 6.80 percent.
Brokers said interest rate uncertainty was likely to linger in the market next week. The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting body next meets on March 25.
"I think it is sideways trading for the time being," said Rossiter.
Shares in HSBC Holdings and Hang Seng Bank were hit hard ahead of the release of their 1996 results on Monday.
HSBC fell HK$2.00 to HK$189.00 and Hang Seng Bank slumped HK$1.75 to HK$89.50.
Shares in Shun Shing Holdings surged HK$1.035, or 104.55 percent to HK$2.025.
COSCO (H.K.) Property Development said on Friday it would raise its stake in the company to 61 percent from 30 percent and make a cash offer for Shun Shing shares at HK$0.72 each.
Shares in Guangzhou Investment fell HK$0.225 to HK$3.925.
The company said on Thursday it would issue 320 million new shares at HK$3.98 each to its parent Yue Xiu Enterprises after Yue Xiu places the same amount of existing shares.
